name: Baccarat
description: Baccarat is the world's most prestigious casino banking game, synonymous with high stakes and cinematic glamour. Though famously complex in its adjudication, the game is mechanically simple for players: they bet on whether the 'Player' hand or the 'Banker' hand will achieve a total closest to nine. In its most popular form, Punto Banco, all decisions are dictated by a fixed 'Table of Play', removing all player agency after the initial bet is placed.

history.origins: Baccarat first appeared in France in the early 19th century, with the earliest known description published in Charles Van-Tenac's 1847 'Album des jeux de hasard et de combinaisons'. Later legends claimed a 15th-century Italian origin, but there is no contemporary evidence for the game before its French documentation.
timeline: 1400s: Early forms of the game appear in Italy.
1800s: Baccarat Chemin de Fer becomes a staple in French underground gambling salons.
1959: Tommy Renzoni introduces Punto Banco to the Las Vegas Sands casino.
1962: Featured extensively in the first James Bond film, 'Dr. No', cementing its luxury status.
history.cultural: Symbolizes extreme wealth and risk; often isolated in 'Baccarat Pits' with higher minimum bets than standard table games.
history.evolution: The game evolved from a player-banked version (Chemin de Fer) where players made choices, into the casino-banked Punto Banco where rules are strictly mechanical.

setup.players: 1 to 14 players. All play against the house bank.
setup.deck: Traditionally 8 decks shuffled together in a 'Shoe'.
setup.dealing: Two hands are dealt: 'The Player' and 'The Banker'. Two cards each to start.
setup.equipment: Standard Baccarat table, dealing shoe, discard rack, commission tracking chips.

rules.objective: Predict which of the two hands will have a total closest to 9.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Place Bets**: Players bet on 'Player', 'Banker', or 'Tie'. 2. **Initial Deal**: Both sides receive two cards. 3. **Naturals**: If either side has an 8 or 9 (a 'Natural'), no more cards are dealt; the higher hand wins. 4. **Player Rule**: If the Player's total is 0-5, they draw a third card. If 6-7, they stand. 5. **Banker Rule**: Follows a complex matrix based on the Player's third card (if any). 6. **Resolution**: The hand closest to 9 wins.
keyRules: Banker Commission: Winning Banker bets usually pay 0.95 to 1 (5% house commission).
Tie Payout: A winning Tie bet typically pays 8 to 1 or 9 to 1.
Push: If a Tie occurs and no tie bet was placed, bets on Player and Banker are returned (Push).

strategy.basic: Always bet on the Banker. Statistically, the Banker wins 50.68% of non-tie hands, and the Player wins 49.32%. Even with the 5% commission, the Banker bet has the lowest house edge.
strategy.intermediate: Avoid the Tie bet. The house edge on the Tie is nearly 14.36%, making it one of the worst bets in the casino.
strategy.advanced: Money Management: Use flat betting. Because there is no skill involved in the cards themselves, focus strictly on managing your exit strategy (Stop Loss and Profit Goals).
tips: Look for 'Reduced Commission' tables (e.g., 4% instead of 5%) to improve your odds.

variations.name: Chemin de Fer
variations.description: The original French version where players take turns acting as the Banker and can decide whether to draw the third card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine models only the Punto Banco betting and draw structure; Chemin de Fer remains a descriptive variation.

variations.name: Baccarat Banque
variations.description: Similar to Chemin de Fer, but the position of Banker is more permanent and follows three columns of cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Baccarat Banque is documented for context; its rotating bank and three-hand structure are not yet encoded as engine overrides.
